workloads.name: cpu_primes
workloads.description: Trial-division prime counting below 300k, range split across threads. Pure bytecode: integer arithmetic and loops, no I/O.

workloads.name: cpu_float
workloads.description: 3M iterations of sin*cos accumulation, range split across threads. Float-heavy bytecode with C-level math calls.

workloads.name: io_sleep
workloads.description: Each thread performs 20 x 10ms sleeps (simulated network/disk waits). The GIL is released while sleeping, so all builds should overlap waits.

workloads.name: contended_list_append
workloads.description: 4M appends to one shared list, split across threads. On free-threaded builds each append takes the list's per-object critical section, so more threads means more lock hand-offs.

workloads.name: contended_dict_update
workloads.description: 2M dict increments guarded by one threading.Lock, split across threads. Measures lock hand-off cost when the GIL is not serialising threads.

workloads.name: mp_primes
workloads.description: Same prime counting as cpu_primes, but using a multiprocessing.Pool (spawn). The classic GIL workaround; includes process start-up cost.

workloads.name: numpy_small_ops
workloads.description: 8 tasks x 20k tiny (256-element) array ops. Python dispatch overhead dominates and holds the GIL, so GIL builds should not scale.

workloads.name: numpy_matmul
workloads.description: 8 tasks x 8 matmuls of 512x512 float64 (BLAS threads pinned to 1). numpy releases the GIL inside BLAS, so all builds should scale.

workloads.name: pandas_groupby
workloads.description: 8 tasks: build a 1M-row DataFrame and groupby-sum. pandas holds the GIL for most of its Cython/Python code.

workloads.name: duckdb_query
workloads.description: 8 tasks: SELECT sum(i*i) FROM range(5M) on a per-task connection with SET threads=1. DuckDB releases the GIL during execution. NOTE: importing duckdb re-enables the GIL on free-threaded builds unless PYTHON_GIL=0 is forced.

workloads.name: sklearn_fit
workloads.description: 8 tasks: make_classification(4000x20) + RandomForestClassifier(20 trees, n_jobs=1).fit + predict. Cython tree building releases the GIL in hot loops.

workloads.name: fastapi_sync_cpu
workloads.description: 32 requests to a sync def endpoint (prime count to 30k) from N concurrent clients; uvicorn runs in a subprocess on the same interpreter. def endpoints run on a thread pool, so free-threading can parallelise them.

workloads.name: fastapi_async_json
workloads.description: 400 requests to a trivial async endpoint from N concurrent clients. Event-loop bound; measures per-request overhead of each build.
